mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off reaction that compresses equity discounting, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by at least 25 bps
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in >70% of triggered events, or FEDFUNDS spikes are not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signal weakening labor market strength, which precedes a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10k while INDPRO decreases by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in >50% of such labor signal events, or correlation between signal and returns is not statistically significant (R² < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) above a 12-month moving average indicates accelerating consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the 12-month baseline (t-test p > 0.05) in >40% of expansionary HOUST periods.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over two consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, which precedes a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls in two consecutive months by >3% each
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain non-negative in >60% of such double-dip INDPRO events, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation acceleration (CPIAUCSL monthly yoy growth > 3%) reduces market expectations for rate cuts, which compresses equity discounting and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL yoy growth exceeds 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative in >70% of such CPIAUCSL episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% triggers a risk aversion cascade that shortens equity discount horizons, resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% by at least 0.3 percentage points
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of such UNRATE events, or the effect is not robust to out-of-sample backtests (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in payrolls (PAYEMS) and retail sales (not available in catalog; substitute with HOUST) over three months signals robust consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not beat the 3-month rolling average in >60% of such dual-proxy demand periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below its 12-month average, without a corresponding decline in payrolls (PAYEMS), indicates supply-side weakness that precedes negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >5% while PAYEMS rises by <2% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of such RSAFS-PAYEMS signal events (p > 0.05).
